# Back to the rule, applied to a real case [20 min]{.time} {#back-to-the-rule}

::: notes
**Goal.** Each doctor runs the three questions on one of their own outputs, decides use, fix or discard, and posts one Monday line.

**Have ready.** One of your own outputs from Days One or Two, open in your assistant, to check on the shared screen as the group checks theirs. Breakout rooms of two (one of three if the count is odd). A tally on the chalkboard (press B): Q1, Q2 and Q3 for "no", then invented, omitted, altered, fabricated citation. For anyone with no output, the referral-letter slide holds a prompt with Case C's facts inside it.

**Watch for.** "It looks right" as the evidence, or "I asked the tool" as the source. The Lab Three output picked again: this round is for the output that looks fine. Real patient detail: stop it and switch to a synthetic case. Tool debates in the synthesis: steer back to the three questions.

**If asked.** Every output at work? Scale to the stakes; anything that goes in a chart or leaves your hands, yes. My honest answer to question 3 is no? That is the signal to slow down, not the finding to accept: verify against the source, or leave AI out of that piece. Everything came out yes? Fine, if question 2's evidence names something you opened; a yes with no evidence is a maybe.

**Bridge.** "You have checked your own work. The last check of the day is on the whole weekend: twenty minutes, all three days."
:::

## One output, checked {#worked-example}

::: {.lane .sm}
[The source]{.node .dark} [An allergy is listed. No timeframe is given.]{.node .same .grow}
:::
::: {.lane .sm}
[The draft]{.node .dark}["Allergies: none known." "...your opinion within two weeks."]{.node .red .grow}
:::

::: {.cards}
::: {.card .red}
[1 · Defend it?]{.t}

No. The allergy line disagrees.
:::
::: {.card}
[2 · Verify it?]{.t}

Allergy: yes, I compared it. Timeframe: no source.
:::
::: {.card .red}
[3 · Catch it?]{.t}

Only with the source beside it.
:::
:::

[Decision: fix]{.pill .teal} [Kind of error: altered, invented]{.pill .teal}

[Illustrative, written for this course, not from a real tool]{.illustrative}

::: notes
**1:00.** **Say.** One way to fill it in, on an excerpt written for this course. The source lists an allergy; the draft says none known, and gives a timeframe the source never mentions. Question 1: no. Question 2: the allergy line, yes, I compared it; the timeframe, no source. Question 3: only because the source was beside it; on a busy afternoon I would have read past it. Decision: fix. Kind of error: altered, and invented. The evidence is what you opened.

**Do.** Talk it through without clicking. This excerpt is illustrative, not a measurement of any tool. Then: "Now yours."
:::

:::

[▲ Each one: yes or no, and the evidence. Then use, fix or discard, and the kind of error.]{.pointer}

::: {.move .solo}
[Solo · 2 min]{.tag} Your own output, the card in your notes. I do the same on screen.
:::

::: notes
**2:15.** **Say.** This is the card from the last slide, for your own output. Mark every number, name, date, dose and source. For each question write yes or no, and the evidence: exactly what you opened. The source is the case or sheet you pasted above the output, in the same chat: not the tool. Finding nothing wrong is a valid result; an empty evidence line is not. Then decide, and name the kind of error. Leave the Monday line for the end. A no is not a failure; it is the check working.

**Do.** Solo: run the check on one of your own outputs on the shared screen while the group runs it on theirs, saying aloud what you mark and what you open. Start a two-minute timer and post "30 seconds left" in the chat. Answer card questions in the chat; do not judge anyone's output.
:::

## Defend it to a colleague {#defend-it}

::: {.lane}
[You: show your marked output and card. Say your decision.]{.node .grow} [↔]{.op} [Your partner: "Where did that come from?" about each mark.]{.node .teal .grow}
:::

[▲ On screen or in the breakout chat. Change your card wherever they find something.]{.pointer}

If you disagree, the source decides: not either of you, and not another AI.

::: {.move .pair}
[Pair · 6 min]{.tag} A breakout room of two. Three minutes each, then swap.
:::

::: notes
**6:15.** **Say.** You checked alone first, so whatever your partner catches is something you really missed. Partner: ask "where did that come from?" about each mark, and point at anything unmarked. Change your card wherever they find something. If you disagree, the source decides, not either of you and not another AI. Swap at three minutes. This is the last breakout step of the weekend.

**Do.** Pair: rooms of two for 6 minutes, with reminders at 3 minutes and 1 minute left. Look in on a few rooms; if you hear "looks right" with nothing opened, ask "what did you open?" **No breakout rooms:** everyone types their decision (use, fix or discard) and the one mark they are least sure of in the chat; read three aloud while the group asks "where did that come from?"
:::

# Assessment quiz [20 min]{.time} {#assessment}

::: notes
**Goal.** Every doctor takes the quiz under the same, clearly stated conditions and knows where to practice afterward.

**Have ready.** Your confirmed quiz sheet: open or closed book, how it is delivered and handed in, what to do when finished. Settle every item before Day Three; the list is in the instructor guide (Open decisions, Assessment). The link to the practice bank on the assessment page, to paste at the end.

**Watch for.** Improvising a policy under pressure: "let me confirm" beats a guess. Hints, and anyone reaching for an assistant by habit: state the rule before it starts. Anxiety: say once that the quiz shows what stuck, not a judgment of them as doctors.

**If asked.** Open book? May I use an AI tool? Pass mark? Will we go over the answers? Answer only from your confirmed sheet; if an item is not confirmed, say so and say when you will tell them. Does the certificate depend on the result? It is a certificate of completion for every doctor who finishes the weekend; anything beyond that comes from the sheet. Can I practice first? The practice bank is separate from the quiz and is for afterward.

**Bridge.** "Quiz done. Ten minutes left: your certificate, four things to keep, and a plan for your first two weeks."
:::

# Certificate and closing [10 min]{.time} {#closing}

::: notes
**Goal.** Each doctor knows what the certificate is, can say the four things to keep, and has written down one low-risk task and one colleague to teach.

**Have ready.** Certificates ready, to be issued by the process on your confirmed sheet. The feedback link, ready to paste in the chat. The closing section of the module page, for the plan's wording.

**Watch for.** A CME, CPD or accreditation claim slipping in, from the group or from you. The closing crowding out the plan: cut "what this course did not cover" to one minute before you shorten the first two weeks. Tool endorsements: the course recommends none.

**If asked.** CME or CPD hours? It is a certificate of completion; the course makes no CME, CPD or accreditation claim, and the accreditation position is in the instructor guide. Which tool on Monday? Whatever your institution approves for patient information; for non-patient tasks, a general assistant you already have; availability changes, so check. Who is responsible if an AI-drafted note is wrong? A medico-legal question outside this course: "AI drafts. You decide" says where the decision sits, not a legal position; ask your data protection officer or legal team. Can I share the site? Answer from your confirmed sheet.

**Bridge.** "Take the low-risk task you just wrote down and run the check on its first output. AI drafts. You decide."
:::

**3:00.** **Say.** Four steps, in order, each small on purpose. At the start of week one, pick one low-risk task, such as rewording an email to a colleague or a first outline for a talk, and run the check on every output; keep patient data out of it. Also in week one, keep a prompt library: prompts that gave a draft you would use, with a placeholder where the facts go, never the facts. Ask your institution whether it has a policy on AI tools and which it has approved. In week two, teach one colleague for ten minutes, on a synthetic case.
